subject: MedSecure pilot: KMS escrow, BYOK options, and subprocessor routing
thread_text:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Legal - MedSecure <legal@medsecure.example.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: MedSecure pilot: KMS escrow, BYOK options, and subprocessor routing

Hi Ana and team,

Thanks again for walking through the pilot scope this week. Per our discussion we dug into three specific asks you raised that affect feasibility and timelines:

1) Customer-managed keys / BYOK (on-hosted or HSM) and escrow requirements
2) Subprocessor residency routing (US-only vs hybrid fallback) and approved cloud providers
3) Evidence and timeline for an addendum combining HIPAA BAA + GLBA clauses for your payments data

I attached a draft DPA (medsecure_dpa_draft_v2.pdf) with placeholders where you asked for specific language. We also attached a brief KMS spec from BlueBridge (bluebridge_kms_spec.odt) to show the integration surface for HSMs.

Quick asks: can you confirm whether escrow requires escrow to a named third party (e.g., a law firm) or whether a sealed key-holding service (KMS escrow via custodian) is sufficient?

Proposed next step: we can run a short security feasibility call w/ BlueBridge (they offer a managed HSM BYOK path) and our infra lead Marcus to map network flows and attestations. Marcus, Priyom — can you both join a 30-min slot next week?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Ana Morales <legal@medsecure.example.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops - MedSecure <ops@medsecure.example.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MedSecure pilot: KMS escrow, BYOK options, and subprocessor routing

Thanks Naomi — good summary. A few clarifications from Legal/Ops:

- Escrow: MedSecure prefers a named escrow agent (we typically use Kessel & Co. for pilots). We do allow custodian models if the vendor provides a legally-binding release flow and audit trail.
- BYOK/HSM: Our security team will accept a hosted HSM with a FIPS 140-2 Level 3 attestation or an on-prem HSM gateway.
- Subprocessors: core PHI processing must be routed to US-only hosts for the pilot; non-PHI telemetry can go to EU if needed, but we want explicit routing rules in the DPA.

We will review your draft DPA and send comments by EOD Wed. For the call, please propose two slots (PST) next week.

Regards,
Ana Morales
Sr. Counsel, MedSecure Health
legal@medsecure.example.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Ana Morales <legal@medsecure.example.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 06 Oct 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MedSecure pilot: KMS escrow, BYOK options, and subprocessor routing

Hi all — quick technical mapping based on Naomi's attachments and BlueBridge spec:

- BYOK approaches we support:
  * Remote HSM (managed by BlueBridge) with delegated key usage tokens
  * Customer-imported key material into our HSM cluster (we support wrapped key import with KMS policy locks)
  * Customer-held keys with an encrypt-only gateway (hardware gateway placed in customer's VPC)

- Escrow implications: if MedSecure requires a named agent (Kessel & Co.), we can automate sealed key deposits tied to DocuSign workflow, but that will need an extra compliance review and a timeline of ~4 weeks for legal + ops to validate.

- Routing: we can pin PHI traffic to US-only zones and configure a strict prefix-based routing policy; fallback (if capacity crunch) goes to a dedicated-reserved GPU pool in US-west. No EU fallback for PHI unless you relax the requirement.

Technical risks: key rotation/rollover during an active session requires coordinated maintenance windows; cross-region failover with BYOK is more complex and will need explicit playbooks.

Proposed call topics: KMS path selection, escrow acceptance criteria + DocuSign automation, DPA clause mapping for routing and attestations.

-Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_kms_byok_matrix.csv

From: Legal - MedSecure <legal@medsecure.example.com>

Cc: Ops - MedSecure <ops@medsecure.example.com>
Date: Thu, 07 Oct 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MedSecure pilot: KMS escrow, BYOK options, and subprocessor routing

Naomi/Marcus — thank you. We reviewed the draft and attached comments (we annotate the PDF). High level:

- MedSecure will accept BlueBridge managed HSM if we receive their FIPS + SOC 2 Type II report and a short runbook describing key custody operations.
- For escrow, Kessel & Co. is preferred. Please confirm you can produce a sealed key deposit and release policy tied to a DocuSign envelope (we can share our template).
- DPA additions: an explicit section that lists allowed subprocessors and a routing table that pins PHI endpoints to US-west/US-east (no automatic failover to EU).

Can you confirm timeline: we need compliance sign-off by Oct 22 to keep the pilot timeline.

Regards,
Ana Morales
Sr. Counsel, MedSecure Health

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Legal - MedSecure <legal@medsecure.example.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, BlueBridge KMS Sales <kms-sales@bluebridge.com>
Date: Fri, 08 Oct 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MedSecure pilot: KMS escrow, BYOK options, and subprocessor routing

Ana — thanks for the speedy review and the annotated PDF (received). Short answers and next steps below:

1) BlueBridge can provide FIPS + SOC2 Type II evidence; I looped their sales contact in to get the artifact and a short runbook. BlueBridge indicated a 5 business-day turnaround for the attestation package.

2) Escrow: we can support a Kessel & Co. deposit flow using an automated sealed-key deposit tied to a DocuSign envelope. Priyom — can you coordinate with Kessel and our legal ops to sketch the integration? I created a HubSpot deal (see link) and attached the most current DPA draft and our BYOK matrix.

3) DPA routing clause: Marcus confirmed we can pin PHI to US zones and disable EU fallback. We will include a routing table in the addendum and a clause for emergency exceptions that require written approval from MedSecure Legal.

Timeline: commit to producing BlueBridge artifacts + escrow runbook by Oct 15; Redwood legal will provide a redline of the DPA incorporating routing and escrow language by Oct 18. If that aligns with your Oct 22 compliance sign-off target, we are on track.

Action items:
- Priyom: coordinate Kessel & BlueBridge discovery (due Oct 12)
- Marcus: produce an ops failover playbook excerpt (due Oct 13)
- Kimberly: prepare DPA redline draft (due Oct 18)

If that looks good I'll schedule a 30-min call for Oct 11 at 10:00 AM PST to walk the artifacts.

Thanks,
Naomi
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: medsecure_dpa_draft_v2.pdf, bluebridge_kms_spec.odt, redwood_kms_byok_matrix.csv
